data.name: Kīpahulu Campground
data.description: The Kīpahulu campground is about 1/8 mile (.2km) south of the Kīpahulu Visitor Center. It overlooks ocean cliffs and is a short walk from 'Ohe'o Gulch. The campground has picnic tables, BBQ grills, and pit toilets. No water is available at Kīpahulu Campground; However, drinking water is available at the Kīpahulu Visitor Center restrooms. There are two general stores in the nearby town of Hāna (10 miles [16km] away) where you can purchase water and basic food supplies.
data.reservationInfo: Reservations are required for all Kīpahulu camp sites.
data.regulationsOverview: Overnight stays are limited to three nights total for all park areas in a 30 day period.

fees.description: Fee for a single campsite reservation.
fees.title: Campsite Fee

fees.description:
All park visitors are required to purchase a recreational use pass upon entering Haleakalā National Park. Passes are non-transferable and are valid for 3 days including the date of purchase. A variety of park passes cover park entrance fees. 

$30.00 per private vehicle - Valid for 3 days.
$25 per motorcycle - Valid for 3 days.
$15.00 per pedestrian or bicycle - Valid for 3 days.

A variety of annual passes are also available, see https://www.nps.gov/hale/planyourvisit/fees.htm for details.
fees.title: Entrance Fee

data.directionsOverview: Kīpahulu Campground is located on the right immediately past the Kīpahulu District Entrance Station. Follow the road .3 mile to the campground loop.

operatingHours.description: Campers will check in at the Kīpahulu entrance station. The check in time is 2 pm. Check out time is no later than 11 am on the last day of the reservation. Campers are expected to leave their camp site neat and litter free for the next visitor.
operatingHours.name: Kīpahulu Campground

images.caption: Find a home away from home at a Kīpahulu campsite.

data.weatherOverview: Kīpahulu Campground is often hot, humid, and buggy. Be prepared for intense rain, sun, and mosquitos when staying at the campground.

accessibility.wheelchairAccess: The campsites are not paved, but vehicles can easily access each individual site in the loop.
accessibility.fireStovePolicy: Fires permitted only in provided grills. Gas stoves are permitted. No ground fires allowed.
accessibility.rvInfo: There are no RV or trailer sites.
accessibility.additionalInfo: Water is available nearby at the Kīpahulu Visitor Center.
accessibility.adaInfo: There are accessible restrooms and water fountains at the Kīpahulu Visitor Center. The campsites are spread out on a flat grassy field, which can be muddy and rocky in places. A small number of sites are .2 mile away from the main campsite loop.
accessRoads: Unpaved Roads - All vehicles OK in good weather

data.name: Hosmer Grove Campground
data.description: Hosmer Grove lies in the cloud belt of Haleakalā, just below the 7,000 foot level (2134m) in the Summit District. Be prepared for rain and cold weather. Nighttime temperatures can drop into the to near freezing (0°C); daytime highs average 50-65°F (10-18°C). The campground has picnic tables, barbeque grills, drinking water, and pit toilets. Overnight stays are limited to three (3) nights total for all Park areas in a thirty day period. Pets are not permitted in or around campsite facilities.
data.reservationInfo: Reservations are required to camp at Hosmer Grove Campground.
data.regulationsOverview: Overnight stays are limited to three (3) nights total for all Park areas in a 30-day period. Pets are not permitted in or around campsite facilities.

fees.description: Fee to reserve 1 campsite for 1 night at Hosmer Grove.
fees.title: Reservation Fee - Per Night

fees.description: All park visitors are required to purchase a 3-day Entrance Pass at the Entrance Gate upon arrival to the park. The campsite reservation does not cover your Entrance Pass. An automated entrance pass machine is available after hours.
fees.title: Entrance Fee - Per Vehicle

data.directionsOverview: Seven hundred feet past the Summit District Entrance Station, turn left at the four-way intersection, following signs for Hosmer Grove Campground. Follow the road for .5 mile to reach the campground parking lot.

operatingHours.description: Hosmer Grove Campground is open year-round.
operatingHours.name: Hosmer Grove Campground

images.title: Hosmer Grove Campground Area
images.altText: A gray tent is pitched next to a grill and picnic table. Tall shrubs and grass line the area.
images.caption: Immerse yourself in the native shrubland of Haleakalā.

data.weatherOverview: The weather in the Summit District can change quickly from warm and sunny to cold and rainy. Hosmer Grove Campground lies in the cloudbelt of Haleakalā, and as such often sees misty, rainy, and wet conditions during winter months and in the afternoons. It is advised to have rain gear and a rain fly when undertaking outdoor activities.

accessibility.wheelchairAccess: There there is one narrow, paved path that leads to the first site only. The campsites are on a sloping, grassy field.
accessibility.fireStovePolicy: Fires are only permitted in designated barbeque grills. Gas stoves are permitted. There are no ground fires allowed.
accessibility.rvInfo: There are not spots available for RVs or trailers.
accessibility.adaInfo: Pit toilet restrooms by the campground parking lot are accessible. There are no designated accessible campsites. The campsites are spread across a sloping, grassy field directly across from the parking lot.

data.name: Wilderness Cabins
data.description: Located on the island of Maui, Haleakalā National Park maintains three wilderness cabins for visitor use-- Hōlua, Palikū, and Kapalaoa. All cabins are accessible only by trail from the summit area and require you to hike a minimum of 3.7 mi (5.9 km).
data.reservationInfo: Reservations are required to stay overnight at any of the three Wilderness cabins.
data.regulationsOverview: Overnight stays are limited to three (3) nights total for all Park areas in a 30-day period.

fees.description: All park visitors are required to purchase a 3-day Entrance Pass at the Entrance Gate upon arrival to the park. A Wilderness cabin reservation does not cover your Entrance Pass. An automated entrance pass machine is available after hours.
fees.title: Entrance Fee - Per Vehicle

fees.description: Fee to reserve 1 Wilderness cabin for 1 night in the Haleakalā crater.
fees.title: Reservation Fee - Per Night

data.directionsOverview: Kapalaoa, Palikū, and Hōlua cabins are located in designated Wilderness. To reach the cabins, you must hike a minimum of 3.7 miles (5.9km) to Hōlua, 5.5 miles (8.9km) to Kapalaoa, and 9.3 miles (15km) to Palikū. All sites are located in the crater of Haleakalā and are accessible from either the Halemauʻu Trailhead (10 minute drive from entrance to the park) or the Keoneheʻeheʻe Trailhead (30 minute drive from entrance to the park).

operatingHours.description: Wilderness cabins are open year-round. Sites may be closed for routine maintenance or resource protection. Closures are displayed on rec.gov.
operatingHours.name: Wilderness Cabins

data.weatherOverview: Cabins are located inside Haleakalā crater and involve a strenuous hike around distinctive cinder cones. Campers should prepare for hot, sunny, cold, wet, and windy conditions as weather can change rapidly. There is no shade or water on the crater floor, and temperatures can vary from 40-70 degrees Fahrenheit during the day and 30-50 degrees Fahrenheit at night, so pack plenty of water, sunscreen, and layers. If it is stormy, winds can exceed 80 miles per hour with temperatures dropping well below freezing.

accessibility.fireStovePolicy: No open fires are permitted in the Wilderness of Haleakalā. Follow posted instructions for wood and propane stove use. Each cabin reservation holder will receive codes via email to access one wood locker per night of reservation that contains three logs for use in the wood stove. Bring a lighter or matches to start the wood and propane stoves. The park cannot guarantee that propane or wood will be available.

data.name: Wilderness Tent Sites
data.description: There are two primitive wilderness tent areas which are accessible only by trail, Hōlua and Palikū. These sites are only reservable on recreation.gov. No first come-first serve sites are available.
data.reservationInfo: Reservations are required to camp at all Wilderness tent sites.
data.regulationsOverview: Camping outside of designated tent sites is prohibited. All tent sites are designated by a brown tent stakes and directional arrows. No pets are allowed on trails or campsite facilities in Haleakalā National Park. Overnight stays are limited to three (3) nights total for all Park areas in a 30-day period.

fees.description: All park visitors are required to purchase a 3-day Entrance Pass at the Entrance Gate upon arrival to the park. The campsite reservation does not cover your Entrance Pass. An automated entrance pass machine is available after hours.
fees.title: Entrance Fee - Per Vehicle

fees.description: When making a reservation online with rec.gov, users will incur an $8.00 service fee. If making reservations using the rec.gov call center, users will incur a $9.00 service fee.
fees.title: Rec.Gov Service Fee

data.directionsOverview: Palikū and Hōlua Wilderness tent sites can be accessed from the Halemauʻu Trailhead (about 10 minutes from the entrance) or the Keoneheʻeheʻe Trailhead (about 30 minutes from the entrance).

operatingHours.description: Wilderness tent sites are open year-round.
